learning_outcomes.text: Knows the fundamental concepts of entrepreneurship and its framework at national and European levels.
Understands the relationship between engineering activity and the valorization of innovations through entrepreneurial initiatives.
Has knowledge about business legislation, intellectual property protection, resources, and business development strategies.
Knows the principles of personal management, career planning, and the development of entrepreneurial skills.
Understands the stages of initiating, planning, and managing a business, including the elaboration of a business plan.
Identifies business ideas and validates their market potential, using economic and legislative analysis tools.
Develops business plans and financing strategies for their implementation.
Applies marketing and promotion concepts for the valorization of products/services.
Drafts relevant documents (business plan, CV, presentation) adapted to the entrepreneurial context.
Actively participates in simulations and practical exercises aimed at initiating and managing a business.
Demonstrates initiative and innovative spirit in identifying and exploiting business opportunities.
Assumes responsibility for substantiating entrepreneurial decisions, respecting ethical and legal principles.
Works effectively in a team, contributing to the development of a constructive and collaborative climate.
Demonstrates autonomy in documenting and applying acquired knowledge to real or simulated situations.
Develops critical thinking and adaptability to the dynamic requirements of the market and economic environment.

syllabus_topics: Subject of study of the discipline.
Introduction to entrepreneurship. Entrepreneur's profile and skills. Principles of personal management. Career strategies.
Business laws. Identifying business ideas. Validating business ideas. Business people's skills. Creating an entrepreneurial attitude.
Notions of economy and economic counseling.
Notions of business legislation and legal counseling.
Notions regarding business initiation. Elements of business idea protection (patenting, trademark registration, logo, etc.) Identifying necessary resources.
Notions regarding business planning, management and establishment. Business plan.
Identifying business financing opportunities. Business financing.
The concept of entrepreneurship. The necessity of entrepreneurship. Entrepreneurial characteristics. Creating a culture for innovative entrepreneurship. Sales laws. Sales strategies.
The necessity of innovation. Barriers and risks of innovation. Innovative projects. Innovative organizations. Business development strategies.
Setting personal goals (specific, positive, SMART, establishing necessary resources).
Developing a career strategy. Preparing a CURRICULUM VITAE.
Simulating the creation of a business plan.
teaching_methods: Lectures include presentations supported by real examples, case study analyses, and guided discussions.
Practical activities based on simulation exercises, role-playing, development of mini-business plans, and solving relevant scenarios.
assessment_rules: The final grade is based on a colloquium (50%) and laboratory activities (50%). A minimum score of 5 (out of 10, likely) is required for both the colloquium and laboratory components to pass the course. All laboratory works must be completed, allowing only one outstanding laboratory work to be recovered.
